defect.summary: op3's resolving-power gate measures 'one record' over a closed vocabulary it chose itself, and names one boundary when both are unresolvable. T18 defined the one-record quantum as the largest |dAMI| from moving one record between OUTCOME cells within its context row. A record is one ROW of the contingency table and a row carries TWO labels; a definition that can only move the right-hand one is a limit of the implementation, not of the question. And when both the floor and the ceiling distance lie inside the quantum, the reader emits ONE reason code and mentions the other boundary in prose.

arbiter.word: I, the arbiter, grant T20: op3-node-response measures what one record can move over every relabel of that record, context as well as outcome, so that the quantum it compares against is never smaller than the record's reach; and when both the floor and the ceiling lie inside that quantum it says so with both reason codes, never one in code and the other in prose.

conditions: 1. The broad move set must CONTAIN the narrow one. A test asserts, on one table, that the broad quantum is greater than or equal to the quantum T18's definition produces. This is the whole correctness argument: it is why adopting the broad reading can only withdraw a verdict and never create one.

2. recomputes === occupied * ((kO - 1) + (kC - 1)), asserted EXACTLY, replacing T18's occupied * (kO - 1). Measured 120 against 15 on a live-shaped 8x2 table with 15 occupied cells. n still drops out of the count; the cheap form is still required and the brute force is still refused.

3. When BOTH the floor distance and the ceiling distance lie inside the quantum, blindReasonCodes carries BOTH codes - OP3_FLATNESS_UNRESOLVABLE_AT_CEILING first, then _AT_FLOOR - and never one code with the other boundary in prose only. The detail string still names which boundary was chosen for the sentence. Two causes, two codes, as T18's own condition 3 already required of the classes.

4. The move string must say whether the winning move was a CONTEXT relabel or an OUTCOME relabel. A quantum whose largest move cannot be identified by axis is a number without a mechanism, and on the measured table the winner was a CONTEXT relabel.
5. No new injected number and no new declaration field. The quantum stays measured from the table.
